Comparative analysis of classical machine learning
and deep learning for galaxy morphology
Two experimental tracks. One question: what can we infer from galaxy images?

Introduce the title as the project umbrella. The evaluated Galaxy10 models classify ten galaxy morphologies, not star versus galaxy. The image is an actual project diagnostic (rendered input and processing views).

Sources: Kishore/results/final/plots/example_1.png
Surveys scale faster than manual inspection
Galaxy structure encodes formation and interaction history.
Labels span smooth, spiral, edge-on, merging, and disturbed forms.
Images contain faint features, varied orientation, and class ambiguity.

Connect morphological classification to population studies. Acknowledge that the example is a project image diagnostic, not a representative sample of each class.

Sources: Kishore/results/final/REPORT.md; Kishore/results/final/plots/example_1087.png
How far can seven interpretable light-distribution and shape measurements take us?
Can a frozen ImageNet representation compete on astronomical images?
What changes when we train the upper CNN layers with galaxy images?
Parallel literature track: reconstruct a Barchi et al. binary SDSS DR7 experiment.

These are comparative questions. The fine-tuned run also changes augmentation and head settings, so we cannot isolate fine-tuning alone.

Sources: comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md; Kishore/paper_replication/results/catalog_dr7_complete_case/REPORT.md
CyMorph measurements joined to GZ1 labels
Kishore: tree, SVM, MLP, majority baseline

Keep both tasks distinct. Barchi reconstruction uses binary labels and catalog features. Galaxy10 uses ten image morphologies.

Sources: comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md; Kishore/paper_replication/results/catalog_dr7_complete_case/REPORT.md
256 × 256 RGB images  •  10 official galaxy morphology classes
Three blank images excluded. Test support ranges from 65 cigar-shaped to 529 round smooth galaxies.

The ten labels are all galaxy categories. Split is object group aware. The original source contains 17,736 rows and three blank cutouts were excluded.

Sources: Kishore/results/final/REPORT.md; Kishore/results/final/class_mapping.json
Group duplicate RGB images or sky positions within 1 arcsec
Five outer folds and three inner folds for RF and frozen CNN
Identical row IDs and labels for all three models
One development fold selected epochs, then refit on all development rows

The 3,545 test rows comprise 3,535 object groups. Do not say fine tuning was nested. Explain duplicate grouping, locked test membership, and a single fold for epoch selection.

Sources: comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md; comparison/three_model/audit/alignment_audit.json

Describe the feature extraction as source detection, sky subtraction, segmentation, aperture/center estimation, then measured light distribution and geometry. Formulas and choices are in METHODS.md and model metadata.

Sources: Kishore/results/final/model_metadata.json; Kishore/METHODS.md
Three-fold inner macro-F1 selected the forest parameters.
Five outer folds estimated development performance.
Final fit: max depth 14, min leaf 2, sqrt features, balanced subsample weights.

Final refit used 160 estimators. Nested CV pooled development accuracy was 53.31%, distinct from 55.26% held-out accuracy.

Sources: Kishore/results/final/REPORT.md; Kishore/results/final/metrics.json
Dropout 0.2; L2 = 10⁻⁴; 18-epoch final head refit. The backbone never updates.

Input is scaled to [-1, 1] after bilinear resize. Global average pooling produces 1,280 features, followed by a regularized linear head.

Sources: Sagar/results/frozen_baseline_full/model_config.json; Sagar/results/frozen_baseline_full/results_report.md
Five candidate head settings; five outer and three inner folds.
Head selection uses development data only and optimizes Macro-F1.
Final head refit uses all 14,188 development galaxies.
No geometric augmentation acts on cached embeddings.

The frozen baseline is a useful test of transferable generic visual features, without astronomical adaptation of the convolutional filters.

Sources: Sagar/results/frozen_baseline_full/results_report.md; Sagar/results/frozen_baseline_full/model_config.json
Final model refit on all 14,188 development images; locked test evaluated once.

Selection used one development fold of 11,349 train and 2,839 validation images. The final refit repeats five warmup and fifteen adaptation epochs with cosine learning-rate decay. Reported results are accepted as supplied.

Sources: Sagar/results/finetuned_mobilenetv2/finetune_config_and_timings.json; comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md
Horizontal and vertical flips preserve the class while varying apparent orientation.
Rotations up to approximately ±90° encourage orientation robust features.
Translations of approximately ±5% vary the object position in the crop.
The held-out images receive deterministic preprocessing only.

Augmentation and partial unfreezing entered the final pipeline together. Their separate contributions were not measured.

Sources: Sagar/results/finetuned_mobilenetv2/README_FINETUNING_ADDENDUM.md; comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md
Dashed line: backbone layers unfrozen after the five warmup epochs.

Validation loss reached its reported minimum of 0.7079 at the selected 15th adaptation epoch; fold validation accuracy was 75.94%. These curves come from Sagar’s supplied experiment.

Sources: Sagar/results/finetuned_mobilenetv2/finetuned_learning_curves.png; finetune_config_and_timings.json
2,702 of 3,545 galaxies classified correctly by the fine-tuned model.

Three test accuracies: 1,959 / 1,997 / 2,702 correct. All aligned by row_id on the same locked holdout. Accuracy axis begins at zero.

Sources: comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md; comparison/three_model/results/comparison_metrics.csv
The gain extends beyond the largest morphology classes.

Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight. Balanced accuracy is mean class recall. All ten classes exist, so macro recall equals balanced accuracy.

Sources: comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md; comparison/three_model/results/comparison_metrics.csv

Values are F1 percentages rounded to one decimal from the exact comparison CSV. The right-hand numbers mark fine-tuned F1. Fine-tuned F1 improves in every class. The cigar class has only 65 test examples.

Sources: comparison/three_model/results/per_class_comparison.csv
Error structure on the locked test

Point to fewer round versus in-between smooth errors, fewer barred versus unbarred spiral confusions, and some persistent tight versus loose spiral errors. Source figure preserves class order 0–9.

Sources: comparison/three_model/figures/confusion_matrices.png; comparison/three_model/THREE_MODEL_REPORT.md
Only 69 of 217 disturbed galaxies were recovered by the fine-tuned model.
Faint tidal structure and overlap with merging systems are plausible sources of ambiguity.
These explanations are interpretations, not separately tested mechanisms.

The fine-tuned disturbed precision is 46.00%. This class improved substantially but remains the lowest F1. Avoid attributing failures to a specific cause without visual adjudication.

Sources: comparison/three_model/results/per_class_comparison.csv; Sagar/results/finetuned_mobilenetv2/finetuned_results_report.md
Frozen vs RF: p = 0.303. Both fine-tuned comparisons: Holm-adjusted p < 0.001.

Exact McNemar on paired correctness; Holm over three row-level accuracy tests. Twenty thousand group bootstrap replicates sampled 3,535 object groups. Bootstrap CIs are marginal. Row-level p-values assume independent row pairs; group-swap sensitivity agrees in direction. Exact adjusted p for fine minus RF 3.0136e-103, fine minus frozen 3.9871e-109.

Sources: comparison/three_model/results/pairwise_statistical_tests.json
Seven interpretable morphology descriptors capture useful structure: 55.26% test accuracy.
Generic ImageNet features deliver a small, statistically unresolved +1.07 point difference.
The complete fine-tuned pipeline raises accuracy by roughly 20 points against either baseline.
Partial unfreezing, augmentation, and head choices changed together.

Say the evidence is consistent with benefits of adapting the full representation. It does not isolate a causal contribution of fine-tuning versus augmentation.

Match exact decimal object IDs to independent Galaxy Zoo 1 E/S labels.
Join DR7 metadata and enforce quality, magnitude, redshift, and K cuts.
Train majority, decision tree, SVM, and 44/88/22 MLP baselines.
Use group-aware nested assessment and a previously inspected holdout.

This reconstructs aspects of Barchi et al. using public catalog data. It does not reproduce the authors’ exact roster or split indices, and the holdout had been inspected earlier. SVM uses fold-local Nyström features.

The 1,049,595-row staged export had 140 conflicting IDs fully excluded; 670,546 author rows matched unambiguous metadata. Separate quality filters and GZ1 labels produce different class proportions.

12 model–cut runs; 60 outer folds. The majority baseline had 50% balanced accuracy.

These accuracies are measured on the DR7 holdouts, not Galaxy10. Rising scores accompany stricter K cuts and changed populations, so avoid interpreting them as pure model improvement. Paper Table 3 is not a matched-test comparison.

Sources: Kishore/paper_replication/results/catalog_dr7_complete_case/REPORT.md

Both examine astronomical morphology classification. Their targets and protocols differ, so comparing 76.22% and 97.22% as model quality would be invalid.

No cross-survey generalization test; class supports are unequal.
Fine-tuned epoch selection used one fold, while both baselines used nested CV.
Augmentation, head settings, and partial unfreezing changed together.
DR7 reconstruction differs from the paper’s roster and prior holdout inspection limits a fresh confirmatory claim.

Sagar’s reported scores are treated as supplied. We have not independently rerun weight-level inference. Discuss if asked; do not frame this as a central result.

The handcrafted baseline is meaningful. Frozen transfer alone adds little.
The full adaptation pipeline produces a large paired gain across classes.
Careful alignment and sample selection determine what a comparison means.

The frozen versus RF confidence interval includes zero. Fine-tuned comparisons have positive group-aware intervals. Close with the distinctions between measured results and plausible interpretation.

Emphasize a true stellar benchmark as a different dataset and task. Cross-survey performance cannot be inferred from in-distribution test scores.
